evidence.claim: Maximus reported FY2025 revenue of about $5.43 billion and described growth in Federal Services as organic, driven by higher clinical program volumes, disaster support, and productivity initiatives.
evidence.source_title: Maximus Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year Results for Fiscal Year 2025

evidence.claim: Maximus fiscal 2025 earnings materials stated that Federal Services revenue increased 12.1% organically and benefited from volume growth across primarily clinical programs and higher-than-typical natural disaster support.

BlackRock reported record assets under management of roughly $14 trillion and substantial net inflows for full-year 2025, supporting its mapping to asset-flow, ETF, fixed-income, and liquidity infrastructure rather than a direct policy-spending node.
evidence.source_title: BlackRock reports record assets under management and increased dividends for full year 2025

evidence.claim: Charles Schwab reported full-year 2025 net interest revenue of $11.75 billion versus $9.14 billion in 2024, and disclosed large Schwab money-market fund balances, making client cash behavior and rates central to the political-rate transmission thesis.
evidence.source_title: Schwab Reports Record 4Q and Full Year 2025 Results

evidence.claim: CME Group reported record full-year 2025 average daily volume of 28.1 million contracts, up 6% year over year, with record annual ADV in interest-rate, energy, agricultural, metals, and cryptocurrency products; Treasury futures and options ADV was 8.3 million contracts.
evidence.source_title: CME Group Reports Record Annual ADV of 28.1 Million Contracts in 2025, Up 6% Year Over Year

evidence.claim: Intercontinental Exchange reported full-year 2025 consolidated net revenues of $9.9 billion, including exchange net revenues of $5.4 billion, fixed income and data services revenues of $2.4 billion, and mortgage technology revenues of $2.1 billion; exchange revenues included energy, financials, data/connectivity, and listings.
evidence.source_title: Intercontinental Exchange Reports Strong Full Year 2025 Results

evidence.claim: United Rentals reported full-year and fourth-quarter 2025 results with rental revenue growth and noted margin pressure from inflation, delivery costs, depreciation, and mix, supporting both infrastructure-execution exposure and cost-risk monitoring.
evidence.source_title: United Rentals Announces Fourth Quarter and Full-Year 2025 Results

evidence.claim: Caterpillar reported that unfavorable manufacturing costs in second-quarter 2025 partly reflected higher tariffs, making tariff policy a direct cost and margin variable for the company.
Caterpillar released its 2025 annual and sustainability reports and stated that 2025 was the highest full-year sales and revenues year in company history.
evidence.source_title: Caterpillar Inc. Releases 2025 Annual and Sustainability Reports

evidence.claim: Jacobs describes itself as having about $12 billion in annual revenue and serving advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, government, and technical consulting markets; fiscal 2025 results referenced strength in Infrastructure & Advanced Facilities and PA Consulting.

Jacobs fiscal 2025 annual report materials identify Infrastructure & Advanced Facilities as a core operating segment, supporting the mapping to infrastructure implementation and advanced-facilities engineering demand.

AECOM reported fiscal 2025 results and said it exited the year with record backlog and pipeline, including a fifth consecutive quarter of sequential backlog growth; total backlog was reported at about $24.83 billion.
evidence.source_title: AECOM reports fourth quarter and full year fiscal 2025 results

memory_update.text: MMS is the cleanest direct policy-implementation name in this chunk: government program administration, clinical assessments, eligibility/benefits operations, and disaster support should be tracked against federal/state contract evidence.

CME and ICE are market-infrastructure mappings, not direct political beneficiaries; the thesis depends on observed rates, Treasury, energy, metals, agriculture, and fixed-income data/clearing volume responses to policy volatility.
URI, CAT, J, and ACM are infrastructure/reshoring execution proxies; they require project-level backlog and end-market validation before they can be treated as chokepoint candidates.

BLK and SCHW should be separated into an indirect macro/liquidity bucket. Their political linkage is mediated by rates, Treasury issuance, ETF flows, cash sorting, and client behavior rather than direct procurement or supply-chain scarcity.
For MMS, J, and ACM, the next evidence layer should collect active federal/state contract awards, backlog by agency or client class, recompete schedules, and any policy-specific volume metrics.
For CAT and URI, evidence must distinguish policy-driven demand from normal construction/mining cyclicality and quantify tariff, inflation, depreciation, and delivery-cost impacts.
For BLK, SCHW, CME, and ICE, market-pricing checks should include valuation, earnings revisions, volume/flow trend data, sensitivity to volatility indices, and rate-path assumptions.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk to policy-transmission nodes. This chunk is mostly indirect or second-order relative to higher-purity defense, tariff, and grid chokepoints. The strongest direct political relationships are MMS to government health/human-services program operations, J/ACM to infrastructure and permitting implementation, and URI/CAT to infrastructure/reshoring execution. BLK/SCHW/CME/ICE are better classified as macro and market-infrastructure relationships: they can monetize Treasury-rate volatility, liquidity shifts, hedging demand, ETF/fixed-income flows, or commodity volatility, but they are not direct policy bottlenecks without flow/volume evidence.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate FY2026 federal and state contract awards, recompete risk, Medicaid redetermination volumes, benefit eligibility rule changes, and segment-level backlog/bookings.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Maximus is mapped to outsourced government health and human-services administration; policy changes in Medicaid, Medicare, eligibility verification, clinical assessments, disaster support, and agency capacity constraints can translate into program-volume and contract demand.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track iShares fixed-income ETF net flows, cash-management AUM, Treasury ETF flows, fee-rate mix, and whether political/fiscal stress is actually increasing BlackRock organic base-fee growth.
ticker_relationships.relationship: BlackRock is mapped as a broad asset-flow and ETF-infrastructure proxy. Federal deficits, Treasury issuance, rate volatility, and liquidity preference can influence fixed-income ETF flows, cash-management assets, and AUM-linked fees, but this is an indirect macro relationship rather than a Serenity chokepoint.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Compare Schwab bank deposit balances, money-market fund balances, net interest margin, supplemental borrowing, cash-sorting trends, and client behavior under current Treasury-rate conditions.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Charles Schwab is mapped to cash sorting, client money-market balances, sweep deposits, and net interest revenue. Fiscal-rate pressure and Treasury yields may alter client cash behavior, but company-specific balance-sheet management and deposit dynamics dominate the relationship.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Monitor monthly ADV by interest-rate, Treasury, energy, agriculture, and metals products; compare volume spikes to tariff announcements, Treasury issuance events, Fed-policy uncertainty, and geopolitical shocks.
ticker_relationships.relationship: CME is mapped to risk-management infrastructure. Fiscal uncertainty, Treasury volatility, tariffs, energy policy, and commodity-policy shocks can raise demand for rates, Treasury, energy, agricultural, and metals futures/options hedging.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track ICE energy transaction revenue, financials volume, fixed-income data annual subscription value, clearing margin balances, and whether political energy/rates volatility is converting to sustained revenue.
ticker_relationships.relationship: ICE is mapped to exchanges, clearing, fixed-income data, and energy-market infrastructure. Political volatility in energy, rates, mortgage policy, and market regulation can support trading, clearing, and data demand; however, the relationship is diversified and lower-purity than direct policy spending nodes.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check rental revenue by end market, large-project demand, specialty-rental growth, fleet productivity, capex guidance, margin pressure, and management commentary on infrastructure and domestic manufacturing.
ticker_relationships.relationship: United Rentals is mapped to execution capacity for reshoring, infrastructure, utilities, energy, manufacturing, and construction projects. Policy can increase demand for rental equipment, but URI is a second-order beneficiary and faces cyclical construction and margin risks.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Separate policy-driven demand from cyclical dealer inventory; verify tariff cost impact, price realization, mining orders, construction backlog, power-generation demand, and regional end-market trends.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Caterpillar is mapped to construction equipment, mining equipment, engines, and power systems tied to infrastructure, strategic minerals, energy, and reshoring. Tariffs can be both demand-supportive for domestic production and a direct cost/margin headwind.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate fiscal 2025/2026 backlog by public-sector and infrastructure categories, federal exposure, contract awards, book-to-bill, and whether permitting/infrastructure policy is producing incremental bookings.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Jacobs Solutions is mapped to engineering, consulting, program management, infrastructure modernization, advanced facilities, and government/regulated project execution. Political funding and permitting reform can support backlog, but post-separation business mix and project-level awards need validation.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track Americas design backlog, government funding exposure, book-to-burn, advisory growth, construction-management strategic alternatives, and evidence that infrastructure appropriations are converting to funded work.
ticker_relationships.relationship: AECOM is mapped to infrastructure consulting, design, advisory, and program management. Public infrastructure funding, climate adaptation, transportation, water, and permitting workloads can support backlog and pipeline, with lower construction-risk exposure than self-perform contractors.
